🚨 Urgent — SPXC halal-breach exit overdue

SPXC's Detection & Measurement segment (Kranze Technology Solutions, $340M defense electronics) trips the no-defense rule. The halal-compliance breach was logged 2026-08-25 and per the standing rule should have meant exit at the next market open, regardless of P&L. Instead it's sitting behind a passive GTC exit-limit at $205 (a profit target) with a $186.90 stop underneath — 13 days later, still held. A compliance breach isn't a price target you wait on.

Action: at Tuesday's open, cancel the $205 resting limit and exit SPXC at market/aggressive limit regardless of where it's trading. Your call, but the rule you set for exactly this situation says don't wait.

⚠️ Data gap today

Live price feed unavailable this run — Yahoo Finance (query1/query2) and the stooq fallback all returned network egress errors, not missing-data errors. No prices were estimated or pulled from search results per policy. Positions table below shows entry/stop/TP from portfolio.json only; confirm current marks in IBKR directly.

For you: keep stops tight and don't add size into this backdrop — Friday's hot jobs report already pushed rate-hike odds up and knocked the S&P/Dow down on the close.

Last historical episodes at this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 COVID bubble peak — see buffett-indicator-history.html.

📰 Position News — Sept 7, 2026

🔵 GOOG

Two live threads: (1) a federal judge rejected the DOJ's push to force a sale of Google's ad exchange — a real antitrust win, removes a structural overhang. (2) Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash plus a new enterprise/government-focused security model, and desks are framing it as "AI spending surge" bullish sentiment into the week. Also: $0.22/share dividend, ex-date Sept 4. Net read: fundamentally constructive, but Friday's tape (hot jobs report, rate-hike repricing) pulled mega-cap tech down across the board — unverified search snapshots put GOOG around $335-338 Friday close, roughly 7-8% under your $364.83 entry. Treat that number as directional only — confirm the real mark in IBKR before acting on it.

🟠 SPXC

No material news since the Q2 print (raised FY26 revenue guidance to $2.705-2.765B on data-center/HVAC demand plus the Neptronic acquisition) — that's already priced in and already known. Nothing new to weigh against the exit decision. The only open item is mechanical: get out, per the alert above.

Not an exit signal by itself, but worth a hold/trim decision on its own merits at Tuesday's open rather than default inertia — especially with the Buffett Indicator at an all-time extreme and Friday's tape risk-off. 💵 Cash Deployment

$330.60 cash available (~$328.60 deployable after the $2 round-trip reserve) — well above the $30 meaningful-position floor, and about to grow further once SPXC's exit clears.

No entry suggestion today: with the live price feed down, I can't derive a real entry/stop/TP order plan for anything (GOOG add-on included), and the "no naked entry" rule means I won't hand you a ticker without one. Markets are closed anyway.

Your call — once prices are back and SPXC is closed out, worth a stock-finder run with the freed cash rather than defaulting back into GOOG.

📚 Today you learned

GTC Orders and Market Holidays

"Good-Til-Canceled" means the order rests until filled or canceled — it doesn't mean it's trying every second markets could theoretically be open. On a day the exchange is fully closed (today, Labor Day), GTC orders simply don't exist as far as the matching engine is concerned; there's no queue, no attempt, no partial check. Your GOOG bracket ($333.90 stop / $408 TP) and SPXC's ($186.90 stop / $205 exit-limit) are both just sitting inert right now, exactly as they were Friday at 4pm ET. They re-arm the instant Tuesday's open auction starts — which matters here because it's also the first moment SPXC's halal-breach exit can actually execute, whether you leave the resting limit or cancel it for a market order.

Also today: Opening auction — like the closing auction, the first trades of the day print through a batch auction (9:30 ET) that aggregates pre-market orders, not a simple first-come first-served match.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Verify halal compliance quarterly on Zoya or Musaffa.
